title: experiment-scheduling-tranches-and-service-impact-matrix
creator: Ava Mitchell
description:
Goal: Define and operationalize a tranchified experiment scheduling and evaluation matrix that ties traffic slices to explicit service impact thresholds and cost/rollback economics. This ticket produces: 1) a schedule template for multi-tranche canaries (timing, traffic ramps, hold windows), 2) an impact matrix mapping experiment surfaces to SLOs and user impact categories, 3) automated gating rules and alert thresholds, and 4) a simple cost/rollback model estimating token spend vs. user risk for each tranche.

Background: Recent canaries for routing and tokenizer changes showed brittle rollouts when downstream latency and billing spikes coincided. We need a prescriptive matrix so PMs/Eng/SREs can pick a pre-approved tranche plan matching expected risk, and a reproducible evaluation window for quality metrics (quality delta, latency P95, error rate, cost per 1k tokens).

Deliverables: 
- Tranche templates: Quiet (0.5% -> 2%), Low (2% -> 10%), Medium (10% -> 40%), High (40% -> 100%) with default time windows (15m/1h/6h/24h) and minimum sample sizes. 
- Impact matrix CSV: experiment surface -> affected SLOs (generation latency, API error rate, token cost variance, tail latency) with severity buckets (none/low/medium/high).
- Gate definitions: explicit numeric thresholds for auto-pass/fail and manual-review gates (e.g., latency P95 increase > +120ms AND error rate +0.5pp => FAIL).
- Rollback economics: break-even cost at which auto-rollback to cheaper model/variant is preferred vs. continuing experiment for quality signal.
- Runbook skeleton and alert playbook for on-call to triage experiment failures.

Acceptance criteria: 
- PM/Eng/SRE sign-off on tranche templates and gate thresholds (documented signoffs in Confluence). 
- A set of Grafana dashboards and alerts are templated and accessible via the experiment run page.
- Automation hooks defined (Terraform/GitHub Actions) to apply tranche-based routing percentages and schedule windows. 
- A documented cost estimation worksheet (spreadsheet) to project token spend per tranche and expected quality sample size.

Metrics & Signals: 
- Primary experiment metrics: quality delta (task-specific eval or prompt-set pass rate), latency P50/P95/P99, user-facing error rate (5xx + structured output failures), per-token cost delta.
- Safety signals: CPU/GPU saturation on Dedicated hosts, KV cache hit-rate regressions, queue length, model OOMs.
- Business signals: CSAT degradation, Checkout failure rate, revenue-impacting endpoints.

Stakeholders: Ava Mitchell (PM), Diego Rivera (Engineering lead), Priya Kapoor (SRE/Oncall), Liam Chen (Design for UX messaging), Zachary Park (Data/Analytics for metric ownership).

Dependencies: 
- ENG-73902 (runtime: scheduled traffic shaper) - needs an API to apply tranche ramps.
- ENG-81814 (console: experiment run page instrumentation) - dashboards and links must exist.
- PM-82401 (evaluation prompt set curation) - gold prompts for quality delta.

Risks & Mitigations: 
- Risk: Small-sample noise causing false-positives in early tranches. Mitigation: require minimum sample size + smoothing windows; default to manual review on marginal fails.
- Risk: Cost spikes when high-traffic tranche overlaps with expensive model variant. Mitigation: cost-breakpoint auto-fallback to cheaper variant and immediate alert to PM/Eng.
- Risk: Alert fatigue from low-signal gates. Mitigation: aggregate signals into composite gate score, instrument runbook for signal triage.

Runbook (high level): 
1) Observe gate failure on experiment run page alert. 
2) Triage - check latency, error rate, token cost panels. 
3) If composite gate score >= fail threshold => auto-rollback if configured; otherwise escalate to PM and SRE. 
4) Apply emergency fallback routing (route to stable model) and notify customers if impacted endpoints match high-risk list. 
5) Postmortem play: capture root cause, update gate thresholds if needed, and rerun with adjusted tranche.

Links & Artifacts: 
- Confluence spec (draft): https://redwood.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/EXP/pages/Tranche+Scheduling+Spec
- Cost worksheet: https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1ExperimentCostModel
- Dashboard template: https://grafana.redwood.company/d/expTemplates/experiment-tranche-overview
- GitHub proto for ramp automation: https://github.com/redwood-inference/ramp-automation/pull/124

Notes for reviewers: 
- I intentionally kept time windows conservative for Medium/High tranches; open to pushing the 6h->12h window if Analytics confirms faster signal maturation for our most common prompt sets. 
- We should decide whether to make the cost-breakpoint fallback opt-in per-project or enforced for all customer experiments.

Next steps:

- SRE to validate metric reliability for early tranche sample sizes (ETA 2026-02-24).
- Prepare dashboard and alert templates (ENG-81814).
